summary: Guidance requested: scheduler bridge (batch->realtime) causing intermittent 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's internal scheduler (cron-driven backfills) occasionally forwards work into the realtime orchestrator bridge which then issues a dense fanout of short-lived inference requests. During these bridge events FluxMetrics sees intermittent 429 responses from the Dedicated pool.

Impact:
- FluxMetrics reports 5-15% request failures as 429 during scheduled bridge jobs (15–20 minute windows).
- Affects user-facing realtime features intermittently as the scheduler backfill overlaps peak traffic.
- Customer uses a Dedicated pool with autoscaling; needs guidance to avoid 429s while keeping cost predictable.

Background / notable config:
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100 nodes reserved, autoscaler enabled for burst to 6 nodes.
- Scheduler job creates 3000 short requests/sec for 90s bursts to warm caches, then stabilizes.
- Scheduler-originated requests currently use same API route/priority as interactive traffic.
- No special burst pool or request tagging is configured.

Customer asks:
1) Recommended configuration to prevent scheduler-bridge traffic from consuming interactive burst credits.
2) Best-practice rate-limit/refill window split for cron-originated warmups vs interactive lanes.
3) Any short-term mitigations to reduce 429s during nightly overlap windows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant with mixed traffic, configure a scheduler to send 3k short requests/sec for 90s to the standard realtime route.
2) Observe rate-limit headers returned on gateway and any 429s in serving runtime logs.
3) During an overlapping steady-state interactive workload (~200 rps), repeat the scheduler burst and measure 429 rate.
4) Toggle scheduler to send same workload to a different route tagged as 'background' and compare results.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:03:14Z rate-limiter: debit_attempt tenant=fluxmetrics amount=3000 result=partial_refill_exhausted window=60s
2026-03-10T02:04:45Z api-gateway: latency spike during scheduler burst p95=420ms p99=1.8s
investigation_notes: Support replicated high-level pattern in staging by running scheduled bursts and saw token accounting attribution to tenant-level burst budget rather than route-tagged budgets.
Rate-limiter logs show scheduler-originated requests use same route key and therefore same refill window as interactive traffic; no separate burst pool exists.
Autoscaler did spin up additional nodes but node arrival was delayed compared to burst duration; autoscale cold-start contributes to pressure.
Hypothesis: two contributing factors — 1) lack of route isolation for scheduler traffic; 2) burst window size too small to absorb short warmup waves.
comments: Support (2026-03-10): Thanks for the report — we can confirm 429s correlate tightly with your scheduler warmup windows. We'll propose a configuration change and short-term mitigation.
Customer (FluxMetrics) (2026-03-10): Priority is to avoid visible 429s for end-users during morning bridge. We're open to separating route or tagging scheduler traffic.

SRE (Liam O'Neill) (2026-03-11): Proposed immediate mitigation: route isolation for scheduler-originated jobs + assign a dedicated low-cost burst pool with longer refill window (e.g., 300s). We'll provide step-by-step commands.
Support (2026-03-12): Attached sample config and rollout steps. We have a follow-up PR to add explicit scheduler-tagging to the ingest orchestrator (see linked PR).
resolution:
Workaround applied: created a separate 'background-warmup' route in the customer's dedicated pool and configured rate-limiter to allocate an isolated burst bucket with a 300s refill window and a smaller sustained window for interactive traffic. Scheduler now calls the background route with an explicit header (X-Redwood-Traffic: background). Autoscaler recommended to pre-warm one node 60s before scheduled run.

Engineering follow-up: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-orchestrator/pull/412 to add header tagging in scheduler; monitoring dashboard added to Confluence runbook.

Next steps: support to monitor nightly windows for 3 days and then consider making the route isolation permanent. Customer accepted workaround and will report back after 3-day observation window.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Background route created and rate-limiter policy applied to isolate refill credits.
2026-03-11: Scheduler configuration updated to target background route header and test burst run executed — 429s dropped from ~8% to <0.5% during test window.
2026-03-12: Monitoring dashboards added to tenant console and Confluence runbook link shared with customer.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add traffic-tagging to scheduler codebase (PR 412) — assigned to Eng team, ETA 2026-03-20.
2) Recommend config doc update for Dedicated tenants to include background route examples (Confluence page updated).
3) Observe production for 72 hours and reopen if >1% 429s during scheduled windows.
